data.text:
The flash floods in Quezon City today reminded me of the Drainage Master Plan that the city through the leadership of Mayor Joy Belmonte had crafted with the University of the Philippines - Resilience Institute to address the perennial problem of flooding or baha.

It's a beautiful plan with the plan containing 3 Volumes and detailed technical studies, analysis, and reports about flooding in the city and proposed solutions, which includes but is not limited to:

1. Water retention ponds
2. Increasing pipe/culvert capacity
3. Waste reduction in channels through netting
4. Channel dredging
5. Detention/impoundment basins
6. Rain harvest systems

The cost of this comprehensive master plan?

27 Billion Pesos.

Compare this cost to the massive 254 projects of the DPWH worth 14 Billion Pesos (for the period 2021-2025) for Quezon City but with nothing to show for it and such projects were not based on or did not apply the principles behind the comprehensive master plan.

As a victim of Ondoy in 2009, I take the corruption of flood control projects personally.

DPWH should just follow Quezon City's master plan and all District Engineers, Regional Directors, contractors, and Congressmen/Senators involved in flood control projects should lay their hands off of it.

And this obviously goes the same to all cities and provinces in the country with a flood control master plan like Pasig City and Marikina City such as the Pasig-Marikina River Basin Flood Control Master Plan pushed for by Mayor Vico Sotto and Mayor Marcy/Maan Teodoro.

Madami na nga ibang blessings na binabaha sa mga Congressmen and Senators, pati ba naman flood control sasawsaw kayo!

#CorruptionControl
#FloodControl
#JoyBelmonte
#VicoSotto

data.text:
Strong winds and heavy rainfall are expected across the North Central Coast region of Vietnam over the next 6 hours⚠️

Tropical Storm Nongfa has developed hours ago, and is currently making landfall over the Vietnam north central coast, in the near exact same location as T5 Typhoon Kajiki just 6 days ago. 
Nongfa only measures T3 on the Devorak scale but is still forecasted to bring wind gusts locally reaching 90 to 100km/h over a few exposed beaches for a few hours. 

Extreme rainfall rates of 1.25 to 1.75 inches per hour are expected for the next 6 hours over the North central coast region, with the weakening system bringing locally torrential rainfall to Central Laos into tonight and eastern/northern Thailand on Sunday. 
Rainfall totals across the regions will vary. 
In Vietnam, heavy rainfall has already fallen for much of the north central coast region, with an additional 3 to 5 inches is generally forecast, as far north as Hanoi. 
Localized amounts of 8 inches is possible in extreme downpours. 
Flash flooding is expected or occurring, landslides are possible in areas of steep terrain. 
But east of the Philippines, Invest 94W and Invest 95W are two tropical disturbances we are also monitoring, which are forecasted to merge this weekend and early next week. 
The system is forecast to track towards Japan in the days following, and is currently granted a 70% chance of development in the next 7 days. 
Japan should remain alert for a potential storm in the coming days. 

And in the eastern pacific, Invest 93E and Dusturbance 2 are being monitored, Invest 93E is granted a 50% chance of development in the next 3 days. 
Disturbance 2 is much closer to Central America, forecast to travel northward. 
The system has a 70% chance of development in the next 3 days. 
By next weekend, twin hurricanes born near the same time may form. 
The Atlantic should remain quite for the next few days. 

Stay tuned for updates! #TropicalStormNongfa #TropicalCyclone #Typhoon #Hurricane #storm
